findings: Owner request 2026-10-29 (BOOK-EXERCISES-01): the chapter 1 exercise (PDF 17-21, printed 14-18) solved in English and Roman Urdu in Practice, like the Computer Science exercises: 16 MCQs (keyed checkpoints), 8 short answer, 12 constructed response, 5 comprehensive (1.3 as parts (a) and (b), so 6 self-checks) and 8 numerical problems. Every printed question is given in the book's words and order; answers are based on the chapter's lessons.
The book prints no MCQ key; every MCQ was worked out. Keys: 1.1 b, 1.2 b, 1.3 c, 1.4 a, 1.5 d, 1.6 d, 1.7 a, 1.8 b, 1.9 d, 1.10 a, 1.11 d, 1.12 d, 1.13 c, 1.14 a, 1.15 a, 1.16 b.
Printed option labels are wrong in three MCQs: 1.2 (a, b, b, c), 1.5 (a, c, d, c), 1.15 (a, c, c, d). The options are listed as a-d in the printed order with a Book correction / Kitab ki ghalti box.

The printed numerical answers in brackets (1.1 9.5 × 10¹⁵ m, 1.2 3.2 × 10⁷ s and 3.1 × 10⁻⁸ year, 1.3 267 cm², 1.4 20.4 kg, 1.5 6.2 ± 0.1 cm³, 1.8 T = constant √(ℓ/g)) were checked and are right; 1.6 and 1.7 are show-that problems. No book correction is needed in the numericals.

Doubtful (diagram readings): the scanned page is about 72 dpi, so the instrument figures are too small to read exactly. MCQ 1.3 (Vernier: main scale 1.4 cm, Vernier 0; only 1.40 cm fits), MCQ 1.4 (screw gauge: the 3.5 mm half-mark is just visible, circular 17: 3.67 mm; 3.17 mm if the half-mark is not uncovered), MCQ 1.14 (positive zero error +0.04 cm, observed 3.30 cm: 3.26 cm), CRQ 1.8 (main 2.7 cm, Vernier 0: 2.70 - 0.02 = 2.68 cm), CRQ 1.9 (main 6.5 mm, circular about 13: 6.63 - 0.02 = 6.61 mm), CRQ 1.11 (main 0 mm, circular 25: 0.25 mm / 8 = 0.031 mm). The figure data read are written in the prompt in square brackets; a reviewer should check them against the printed book.
Unclear superscripts in the scan: short answer 1.4(b) read as 206.4 × 10², 1.5(a) as 580 × 10² g and 1.5(b) as 0.45 × 10⁻⁶ s; answered on these readings.

Beyond the chapter: the Vernier Callipers and the screw gauge (short answer 1.3, MCQs 1.3, 1.4, 1.14, CRQ 1.7-1.9, 1.11) are not described in this chapter; their answers use the usual least-count and zero-error rules and are labelled "(beyond the chapter)" where a definition is asked. CRQ 1.3 (why the kilogram is the base unit) is also beyond the chapter's text. CRQ 1.11 assumes the usual least count 0.01 mm (not printed) and reads "folds three times" as 8 layers; comprehensive 1.3(b) assumes least counts 0.01 g and 0.01 cm (not printed), as in Example 1.3.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
